label: Appendix A: Overview and Index
notes: This short appendix, printed pages 574 through 582, is a toolbox rather than a theory. It assembles the smooth-map machinery that later isotopy, gluing, and moduli arguments quietly assume. Treat this opening slide as a map: each later tool is previewed here and pointed back to where the main text spends it.

label: Why an Appendix on Smooth Maps
notes: Students often forget that symplectic constructions lean on analysis. Moser isotopy, neighbourhood theorems, and gluing all need smooth functions built to order. The appendix isolates that analysis so the main chapters stay geometric. Stress that nothing here is symplectic; it is the differential-topology plumbing that makes the geometry run.

label: Smooth Maps Between Manifolds
notes: Recall the chart definition: a map is smooth when its coordinate representatives are infinitely differentiable. The appendix reviews this only to fix notation and to prepare the harder corner case. Emphasise that smoothness is a local, chart-checkable condition and that diffeomorphisms are the isomorphisms organising the whole theory.

label: Manifolds with Corners
notes: The genuinely new object is a manifold with corners, modelled locally on a quadrant. Walk the index of strata: interior, codimension-one faces, codimension-two corners. The depth of a point counts how many coordinates vanish. This stratified picture is exactly what compactified moduli spaces of holomorphic curves carry.

label: Why Corners Arise
notes: Corners are not pathology; they are forced. A product of two manifolds with boundary already has a corner along the product of the two boundaries. Moduli spaces of pseudoholomorphic curves degenerate by bubbling, and the strata fit together as corners. Motivate the abstraction by these two unavoidable sources.

label: The Standard Smooth Bump
notes: Everything constructive flows from one function: exp(-1/x) on the positive axis, zero elsewhere. It is smooth but not analytic, flat to infinite order at the origin. From it we cut, paste, and interpolate. Have students verify that every derivative vanishes at zero, killing any hope of a Taylor series.

label: Bump Functions and Cutoffs
notes: Stretching the basic germ gives a plateau: a smooth function equal to one on a ball and zero outside a larger ball. These cutoffs let us localise any construction. Underline that compact support plus the value-one core is the engine behind every gluing and extension argument that follows.

label: Partitions of Unity
notes: Partitions of unity turn local data into global objects. Subordinate to a locally finite cover, the bump functions sum to one, so locally defined metrics, connections, or sections average into a global one. This is the single most reused tool in the appendix; flag every later existence proof that secretly invokes it.

label: Extension Lemmas
notes: The extension results say a smooth map or section defined near a closed set extends smoothly to the whole manifold, in the Whitney spirit. The proof glues a local extension to the original using a cutoff. Point out that this is how neighbourhood theorems promote germ-level data to honest global maps.

label: How the Toolkit Is Spent
notes: Close by spending each tool. Bump functions and partitions of unity build the symplectic forms and almost complex structures of earlier chapters; extension lemmas drive Moser and neighbourhood arguments; corners organise moduli compactifications. The appendix is an index, so end by sending students back to those exact call sites.
